_comment: Pure white-space research for the Denmark region. Each institution here was checked against every Danish-realm Elsevier Pure portal (14 found, listed in _method.portals) plus its own domain and a <slug>.elsevierpure.com lookup, and showed no Pure tenancy. Contacts are the people who hold research-information budget or influence: rectors/CEOs, research directors, library and research-support leads, data/IT leadership and AI teams. emailStatus 'published' = the address is printed on the cited page; 'constructed' = built from the institution's visible address pattern and NOT yet verified. Extend via scripts/discover-staff.js, which now carries these institutions in data/staff-sources.json. Addresses on Cloudflare-obfuscated pages (DIGNITY) were decoded from the page's own data-cfemail attributes, which is what the page's script does in a browser.

_method.universe: OpenAlex institutions in DK/GL/FO (726 distinct), filtered to 194 non-company organisations with >=200 indexed works.
portals: adk.elsevierpure.com (Royal Danish Academy + Design School Kolding + Aarhus School of Architecture)
_method.negativeTest: 4,885 organisation names were enumerated across those portals via each portal's /en/organisations/?format=rss feed and matched against every candidate name and OpenAlex alias; a candidate also had to have no resolving <slug>.elsevierpure.com host.
_method.ruledOut: NFA (nfa.elsevierpure.com) and GEUS (pub.geus.dk) were on the draft list until the hosted-tenant check found live Pure instances - both are customers, not white space. University of the Faroe Islands, Rigsarkivet, Moesgaard Museum, Naturhistorisk Museum Aarhus and Kong Christian X's Gigthospital were likewise removed after they turned up inside a consortium portal.
_method.companyTypeSweep: OpenAlex types 234 Danish organisations as 'company', which the >=200-works non-company screen excluded wholesale - the reason SEGES was initially missed. All 63 company-typed organisations with >=200 works were reviewed: Bioneer and Det Danske Sprog- og Litteraturselskab are research institutions mis-filed as companies and were added; DELTA is defunct (merged into FORCE in 2017); IPU restructured in 2022 into a grant-making foundation plus a commercial P/S; Dansk Gasteknisk Center is an a/s owned by the grid operator Evida; Syddansk Innovation no longer resolves. The remainder are genuine commercial firms and are deliberately excluded - Pure is sold to research institutions, so listing pharma and engineering companies would dilute the prospect list rather than extend it.
_method.affiliationRule: Appearing as an organisation inside another institution's Pure is treated as coverage through a partner, not as a tenancy, and does not remove an institution from this list. Applied to the three regions (whose clinicians publish into university Pures) and, from 2026-09-12, to Alexandra Instituttet, whose organisation page sits in AU's Pure. The test for having Pure is a portal or hosted tenant the institution itself operates.
_method.scopus: Scopus has a public register. The Royal Danish Library's national consortium agreement with Elsevier for 2025-28 (pro.kb.dk) enumerates every Danish account and its ECR id; it lists 16 Scopus accounts, which expand to 34 tracked institutions once a university account's named university hospital and its own research centres are included. Absence from that register is real evidence, because the consortium is how essentially every Danish public research institution buys - but it is not proof: an institution can contract directly with Elsevier, and the register would not show it.
_method.scival: SciVal appears nowhere in the national agreement - it is not a consortium product, so every SciVal sale is direct and there is no register to check. Two things are still usable: a library or research-support page naming SciVal is positive evidence (found for six institutions), and SciVal is an analytics layer over Scopus, so an institution with no Scopus is not running SciVal either. That leaves the institutions that hold Scopus but show no SciVal evidence genuinely open rather than confirmed-absent - they are marked unverified, and they are the best prospects, since the prerequisite is already paid for. Parent inheritance applies to SciVal exactly as it does to Scopus: a university hospital or university-owned research centre works off its parent's licence, so 17 such units that first showed as unverified are recorded as covered.
_method.scivalCaveat: A site crawl of all 73 institutions for the words Scopus and SciVal was run and then discarded as evidence: it returned only two Scopus hits and no SciVal hits, missing even KU and AU, whose library pages sit deeper than the crawl reached. It is recorded here so the negative result is not mistaken for a finding.
_method.wos: Web of Science is Clarivate's, so it is tracked here as the competing product rather than as something to sell: an institution running WoS is a displacement target for Scopus and SciVal, not white space. Det Kgl. Bibliotek does hold a national Clarivate agreement for Web of Science Core Collection (listed at https://pro.kb.dk/licensservice/videregaaende-uddannelser/aftaler), but unlike the Elsevier agreement it publishes no participant list, so there is no register to enumerate subscribers from and no reliable negative test. Status is therefore only asserted where an institution's own library pages confirm it. All eight prior wos:'yes' claims were re-checked against their cited proof: seven still hold (KU, AU, DTU, SDU, AAU, CBS, RUC — AAU's is a PDF and was confirmed by extracting its text), and ITU's was refuted. The remaining institutions are left unknown rather than counted as white space.
_method.wosFinding: Every confirmed Web of Science subscriber also holds Scopus, so no institution in the 39-strong Scopus white space is a known WoS displacement target — on current evidence that list is a greenfield opportunity rather than a competitive fight. That conclusion is bounded by the institutions whose WoS status is unknown, which is most of them.
_method.dimensions: Dimensions is Digital Science's, so like Web of Science it is tracked as a competing product rather than as white space. There is no national agreement for it — Digital Science, Dimensions, Altmetric and Figshare appear nowhere in Det Kgl. Bibliotek's consortium agreements — so every subscription is direct and there is no register. Detection is further complicated by a large free tier: the free Dimensions app is open to anyone, and only Dimensions Analytics is the paid product, so an institution merely naming Dimensions proves nothing. Status was therefore taken only from how an institution's library links it. KU links it through a Royal Danish Library Alma catalogue permalink exactly as it links Scopus, and the catalogue shows it as a held Digital Science e-resource — that is a subscription. OpenAlex, by contrast, gets a direct link to the free site, which is how a free resource is treated. RUC publishes a comprehensive bibliometrics guide naming Scopus, SciVal and Web of Science but not Dimensions, so it is recorded as absent. Every other institution is left unknown: their pages cover one product rather than the full toolset, so absence there proves nothing.
_method.cris: Converis (Clarivate) and Symplectic Elements (Digital Science) are CRIS systems, so they compete with Pure, not with Scopus or SciVal, and are treated as displacement signals on the Pure tab. Neither has a Danish footprint. A university-library sector report on CRIS (https://findresearcher.sdu.dk/ws/files/173424165/PSG_2020_2_Online_Bilag_2_CRIS_rapporten.pdf) names Pure 1,073 times across 245,000 characters and Converis, Symplectic, Elements, VIVO and Esploro exactly zero times, and states that every Danish university runs the same CRIS — "alle universiteter i dag det samme CRIS" — each under a service agreement with Elsevier. Status is then set by rule rather than by guess: an institution runs one CRIS, so wherever Pure is installed Converis and Symplectic are recorded as absent, and the same applies at Forsvarsakademiet, which runs Esploro. Institutions with no known CRIS at all are left unknown.
_method.crisSweepDiscarded: Two automated sweeps for competing CRIS portals were run and discarded. The first reported zero rivals but failed every positive control, missing KU's Pure, DTU's Orbit, AAU's VBN and FAK's Esploro. The second, with broader link-following, found FAK's Esploro but still missed three of four controls, because CRIS portal hostnames (researchprofiles, orbit, vbn) cannot be derived from an institution's domain. Discovery, not fingerprinting, was the weak step. The sector report above is used instead, and the sweep results are recorded here only so their emptiness is not mistaken for evidence.
_method.wosDimensionsRemainder: An attempt to resolve the remaining Web of Science and Dimensions unknowns established only what inheritance could give: eleven university-owned research centres for Web of Science and five for Dimensions, on the same rule used for Scopus and SciVal. The rest could not be resolved from public sources and are deliberately left unknown. Neither product has a public subscriber register in Denmark, and three separate website crawls were built and discarded, each failing its positive controls — the last could not find Web of Science on KU, CBS or RUC, all of which demonstrably have it, because Danish institutional sites are JavaScript-rendered and do not expose their database lists to link-following. University hospitals were also left alone: the Elsevier agreement names them explicitly for Scopus, but no equivalent document scopes Web of Science or Dimensions to them, so inheriting would be an assumption rather than a reading. Settling the remainder needs Clarivate and Digital Science account data, or a person checking each library's A-Z list by hand.
